skill.name: mantis-threat-model
skill.description: Builds a Markdown threat model from existing Mantis architecture and entity documentation, including trust boundaries, threat actors, deployment intent, and snapshot provenance.
skill.summary: Turn an existing Mantis knowledge base into a versioned threat model with explicit trust boundaries and attacker profiles.
skill.author: google

security_audit.summary: All 101 static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, expected workspace metadata, or locator checks skipped by this KB-only stage. No evidence found of credential theft, exfiltration, malicious execution, or audit-directed prompt injection. One semantic finding identifies potential archive-history loss when the same pass is rerun.

remediation.issue: Repeated runs with the same pass number can replace an existing archived threat model.
remediation.suggestion: Preserve existing pass archives or use unique revision filenames, and verify successful archival before replacing the live model.

semantic_findings.title: Repeated Passes Can Replace Archive History
semantic_findings.description: The same pass number selects the same archive filename on repeated runs. Copying the current model there can replace earlier history without a collision check.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The procedure explicitly copies to a pass-number filename but provides no protection for an existing archive. This establishes a potential history-loss risk, not observed exploitation.

content.user_title: Build Threat Models from Your Mantis Knowledge Base
content.value_statement: Architecture notes often leave attacker access and trust boundaries unclear. This skill turns existing Mantis knowledge into a structured threat model with deployment intent and snapshot provenance.
actual_capabilities: Read existing architecture and entity documents to identify exposed components and trust boundaries.
Describe threat actors, reachable attack vectors, and high-risk assets with links to relevant entities.
Classify deployment intent using five production-signal checks and default to production when evidence is uncertain.
Assign availability tiers to assets using existing knowledge base evidence.
Stamp the model with snapshot provenance and mark reused content as stale.
Copy the previous model to a pass archive before saving the replacement Markdown document.
limitations: Requires an existing, populated Mantis knowledge base; it does not inspect target source code or extract JSONL learnings.
Model accuracy depends on the completeness and correctness of architecture and entity documents.
Snapshot labels record supplied or stored metadata; this stage does not verify the target source snapshot.
Repeated runs with the same pass number can replace an existing archive unless additional protection is applied.

use_cases.title: Review Architectural Exposure
use_cases.description: Identify attacker entry points and trust boundaries from an existing Mantis architecture knowledge base.

use_cases.title: Refresh Models After Snapshot Changes
use_cases.description: Regenerate threat-model sections and reassess deployment intent when the recorded snapshot changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare Security Planning Context
use_cases.description: Provide downstream planning agents with attacker profiles, entity references, and asset availability classifications.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Initial Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Run /mantis-threat-model using the populated Mantis knowledge base in the current workspace.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: generate the first model from prepared KB documents.

prompt_templates.title: Use a Separate State Directory
prompt_templates.prompt: Run /mantis-threat-model --state_root [state_directory]. Use its architecture and entity documents, archive the prior model, and save the replacement.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: keep knowledge base state separate from the current directory.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh for a New Snapshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Run /mantis-threat-model --state_root [state_directory] --snapshot_id [snapshot_id]. Recompute deployment intent when provenance changes and default to production for uncertain evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: refresh threat-model context after a snapshot update.

prompt_templates.title: Review Reuse and Archive Integrity
prompt_templates.prompt: Run /mantis-threat-model --state_root [state_directory] --snapshot_id [snapshot_id]. Preserve existing archives; add the required STALE banner if unchanged provenance leads to reused content.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: manage repeated passes without silently losing archive history.

output_examples.input: Generate a model from a KB describing a public API, an authentication service, and a customer database.
output: System overview: The public API accepts client requests and delegates identity checks to the authentication service.
Deployment intent: Production, because the KB describes an externally reachable service.
Trust boundary: Untrusted requests cross into authenticated application operations at the API authorization layer.
Threat actor: An unauthenticated network attacker can reach the API entry point.
High-risk asset: Customer records require confidentiality and integrity protections.

output_examples.input: Rerun the model using the same recorded snapshot and reuse the existing model content.
output: Snapshot provenance: The model retains the current snapshot identifier.
Freshness warning: The threat model was not reevaluated this pass and was carried forward from the unchanged snapshot.
Archive action: The prior model is copied to the pass archive before replacement.

best_practices: Populate architecture and entity documents with current deployment, entrypoint, and availability evidence before running the skill.
Keep snapshot identifiers consistent with the knowledge base revision and review models marked stale.
Preserve existing pass archives and verify the backup before replacing the live threat model.
anti_patterns: Using this skill as a source-code scanner or JSONL learning extractor.
Declaring a system sample-only when production evidence is missing, contradictory, or uncertain.
Treating unchanged snapshot labels as proof that the knowledge base is current or rerunning passes without archive protection.

faq.question: What inputs does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires populated Mantis architecture and entity documents. Workflow state and an existing model provide optional pass and provenance metadata.

faq.question: Does it inspect application source code?
faq.answer: No. This KB-only stage reads synthesized architecture and entity documents, not target source code or raw JSONL learnings.

faq.question: Where is the threat model saved?
faq.answer: It saves THREAT_MODEL.md in the selected state workspace KB and copies the previous model into the pass archive.

faq.question: What happens when snapshot metadata is missing?
faq.answer: Without an explicit snapshot identifier or pinned state metadata, it uses UNPINNED provenance and rederives the model.

faq.question: How does it classify deployment intent?
faq.answer: It allows sample-only classification only when all five production-signal checks pass. Any uncertainty requires production classification.

faq.question: Can repeated runs affect model history?
faq.answer: Yes. Reusing a pass number can replace its archived model. Preserve existing archives before rerunning the same pass.
